column1: # Archy owns this list. The publisher reads it when it copies the GitHub tree.
# One folder per line, tab-separated: path, the line GitHub shows, the longer note.
# The line stays when that folder changes. The Archy version and the change go under it.
# Add a row when a new folder joins the public tree.

column2: The five programs: screen, brain, mothership, trade book, and version window.
column3: Matrix is the operator screen, Spring is the hunter brain, Meta is the mothership, Pettibon is the saved trade book, and Archy is the version window. Hummingbot, the trading engine, is not in this folder.

column2: Archy records each change. The operator levels up and sends to GitHub.
column3: A bump adds the next g number and refreshes this tree on the machine. It does not push. LEVEL UP and the second GitHub click belong to the operator.

column2: Matrix is the operator screen. It does not send an exchange order.
column3: The native desk and the web wire live here. Spring writes the hunter files. The hunter does the trade. Connector keys stay on the machine.

column2: Native desk for Home, Wire, Hunters, and Funds. Build it with make.
column3: X11 window. The wire connects a shared Hyperliquid subaccount pool to any controller. The desk does not sign an order.

column2: Web wire and the Flask pages. Keys stay on the machine.
column3: The browser wire and the hunter pages. A wallet on the wire is a subaccount name. The key paste stays on the local Confiig page.

column2: Meta lists the matrices and can push a build. It does not close a clip.
column3: The mothership window. It shows which matrix is behind. It does not move funds and it does not flatten a position.

column2: Pettibon stores the trade book. It does not place an order.
column3: It watches one hunter and writes the book. Grafana can read that book. Pettibon does not send a trade.

column2: Spring is the hunter brain on port 5004. It writes hunter files.
column3: The matrix, Meta, and Archy talk to Spring. A bias change does not close a clip. Spring does not sign a Hyperliquid order.

column2: Windows bundle. Docker runs Hummingbot, the hunters, and Spring.
column3: Start with up.bat or up.sh. That asks for the risk notice first. Wallets and the install password are not in this folder.

column2: Notes for the desk build and the printed wire pages.
column3: How the programs fit together, and the scripts that make the printable pages.

column2: How the desk, Spring, and Meta are compiled and how the files fit.
column3: Compile notes and the file map for the C++ programs. The running machine keeps its own folders.

column2: Scripts that build the printable wire pages.
column3: Local print helpers. They do not talk to an exchange.

column2: Hunter scripts that run inside Hummingbot. The engine is not in this repo.
column3: One script for each hunter container. Shared pieces cover leverage, the risk skim, and the matrix store. Wallets and connector files are not here.

column2: Installer for a Linux machine. The risk notice is required before start.
column3: Installs the desk, Spring, and the hunters. Hunters start only after the risk notice is accepted. The install password is not in the preseed.

column2: Scripts for the Mint USB image. The install password is not here.
column3: Builds and writes the rimBaud look onto an official Mint image. First boot asks for a new password.

column2: Side services that sit next to the five programs.
column3: Condor gauge and the version page. Neither one is a hunter.

column2: A small gauge beside Condor. Condor is Hummingbot's own screen.
column3: rimBaud does not replace Condor. This folder is only the gauge that can sit next to it.

column2: The version page. It reads the Archy version.
column3: Shows the published version. It does not deploy and it does not trade.

column2: Libraries shipped beside rimBaud. Their own licenses stay.
column3: Nothing in this folder is rimBaud code. Keep the upstream license with the upstream file.

column2: nlohmann JSON, MIT, for the C++ programs. This is not rimBaud code.
column3: Single-header JSON library, version 3.11.3, Copyright Niels Lohmann. The MIT license stays on the header.

column2: Helpers: the publisher, the telegram sender, and the wallet creator.
column3: Tools that build or notify. They are not hunters. Secrets are not in this folder.

column2: Sends a short note to Telegram. The bot token is not in this folder.
column3: One sender script. The token stays on the machine that runs it.

column2: Creates a Hyperliquid wallet on the user's own machine.
column3: The new key stays where the user creates it. This folder does not contain a key.

column2: WireGuard enrollment between matrices. Live keys are not in this folder.
column3: Sets up the link a remote matrix uses. Private keys are created on the machine, not stored here.
